title: Ukraine hits key Crimean bridge, curbing traffic, Russian governor says
html:
A Russian Navy amphibious landing ship that was deployed to transport cars across the Kerch Strait, moves near the Crimean Bridge, a section of which was damaged by an alleged overnight attack, as seen from the city of Kerch, Crimea, July 17, 2023. REUTERS/Alexey Pavlishak

MOSCOW, Nov 16 - Ukraine has struck the bridge linking Russia and Crimea across the Kerch strait, limiting the flow of traffic, the peninsula's Russian-backed governor Sergei Aksyonov said on Monday.

Europe's longest bridge connects Russia with the Crimean peninsula, seized by Russia from Ukraine in 2014. It is widely viewed as one of Russian President Vladimir Putin's signature infrastructure projects.

Aksyonov gave no details of the damage in a statement on messaging app Telegram, but said traffic on the bridge would be limited until midday on Monday.

The bridge has come under attack by Ukraine several times since the outbreak of full-scale war in 2022, including a truck bomb that October which killed four and limited capacity for several months.

Monday's attack came as Russia has intensified strikes on bridges in Ukraine, including the capital Kyiv, in the past few months. REUTERS
summary: MOSCOW, Nov 16 - Ukraine has struck the bridge linking Russia and Crimea across the Kerch strait, limiting the flow of traffic, the peninsula's Russian-backed governor Sergei Aksyonov said on Monday.
